_comment: Tracked provenance for the Fresh38 capture harness (AIOS-RUNTIME-RELIABILITY-01, CL-03).
History. The wrapper originally preferred an opaque session-scratch copy of the runner
back to a copy under .artifacts/. Both happened to be byte-identical, but nothing checked that,
so a canonical qualification run depended on a file nobody could verify. FIX-MEAS01 pinned the
identity here and made a mismatch abort the capture.
CL-03 finishes the job. Hash pinning proved the runner had not changed, but the bytes still lived
only under .artifacts/, which is gitignored (/.artifacts/), so a fresh checkout could not
reconstruct the harness at all. The canonical source is now scripts/fresh38/, which is tracked.
A fresh clone contains the exact runner bytes, and the hashes below are verified against them at
There is exactly one canonical source. The .artifacts copy is a leftover runtime artifact: the
wrapper no longer reads it, and if it exists and differs from the tracked source the wrapper says
so in capture.log rather than letting the two drift unnoticed.
To intentionally change the harness: edit scripts/fresh38/, update the hash here in the same
commit, and state why. Never edit this file to make a failing capture pass.

deprecated_copies.note: gitignored runtime artifact, byte-identical at the time of the CL-03 migration; no longer read by the wrapper
original session-scratch copy; retained only as historical evidence
